The '''Rosenau–Hyman equation''' or '''''K''(''n'',''n'') equation''' is a [[Korteweg–de Vries equation|KdV-like]] equation having [[compacton]] solutions. This nonlinear [[partial differential equation]] is of the form<ref>{{citation | first1=Andrei D. |last1=Polyanin |first2=Valentin F. |last2=Zaitsev |title=Handbook of Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations |date=28 October 2002 |edition=Second |page=891 |publisher=CRC Press |isbn=1584882972  }}</ref>

: <math> u_t+a(u^n)_x+(u^n)_{xxx}=0. \, </math>

The equation is named after [[Philip Rosenau]] and [[James (Mac) Hyman|James M. Hyman]], who used it in their 1993 study of compactons.<ref>{{citation | last1=Rosenau | first1=Philip | last2=Hyman | first2=James M. | title=Compactons: Solitons with finite wavelength | publisher=American Physical Society | year=1993 |journal= Physical Review Letters |volume= 70|  issue=5 | pages=564–567 |doi= 10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.564 | bibcode=1993PhRvL..70..564R | pmid=10054146}}</ref>

The ''K''(''n'',''n'') equation has the following traveling wave solutions:
* when ''a''&nbsp;>&nbsp;0

:: <math> u(x,t)= \left( \frac{2cn}{a(n+1)} \sin^2 \left(\frac{n-1}{2n}\sqrt{a}(x-ct+b)\right)\right)^{1/(n-1)}, </math>
*when ''a''&nbsp;<&nbsp;0
:: <math> u(x,t)=\left( \frac{2cn}{a(n+1)}\sinh^2\left(\frac{n-1}{2n}\sqrt{-a}(x-ct+b)\right)\right)^{1/(n-1)}, </math>

:: <math> u(x,t)= \left( \frac{2cn}{a(n+1)} \cosh^2 \left(\frac{n-1}{2n}\sqrt{-a}(x-ct+b)\right)\right)^{1/(n-1)}. </math>
